title: The Last Bid
logline: At a dawn fish auction, a buyer who comes every morning for a particular catch loses it, again, to a higher bid.

object.note: Object 2 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Wanting refused, again: from the full train at the city station to a lagoon-side auction where a regular buyer's catch goes to a higher bid.

thread_out.thread: The catch that went to someone else becomes a net cut by someone else: blocked wanting starts to push back, and the heat of the next stage begins on another shore.

requirements: An active fish auction with a genuine daily market
A regular buyer willing to be followed over more than one morning
Permission to film inside a working market at trading hours

lesson.in_simple_terms: Coming back every morning takes effort and resolve, and the texts say effort is not the same as greed. When someone else bids higher, even a well-practised wanting simply hits a wall.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: සෑම උදෑසනකම නැවත නැවත පැමිණෙන උත්සාහය ලෝභයම නොවන නමුත්, වෙනත් අයෙකු වැඩි මිලක් කී විට ඒ උත්සාහයත් හිස් අතින් නැවතේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma counts earning, guarding and spending wealth among the everyday occasions of greed-rooted minds, but also says the same work done with practical wisdom, with regard to what is useful, is not counted as unwholesome. Effort (vīriya) is described as the mental quality that does not turn back until a task is done, and decision (adhimokkha) as the mind settling firmly on an object, rightly or wrongly. The texts insist these factors have no moral colour of their own: they take on the quality of the mind they join.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The auctioneer's fast calls and the buyers' hand signals make each decision visible at the moment it is made. The regular buyer's face as a bid passes their limit, and the catch carried off by someone else, let the viewer feel resolve meeting a wall, with no voice telling them what the buyer should feel.
lesson.caution: This does not mean that hard work always pays off or is always good: the texts treat effort and decision as forces that can serve harm as easily as good, and a firm decision can be a wrong one.
lesson.builds_on: The last film showed ordinary wanting refused by a changing board; this one shows it refused by someone else's stronger want, and adds that the resolve behind it was never the same thing as greed.
